gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 identifies the same failed homotopy construction: affine interpolation of circle-valued representatives is not well-defined, and a coherent global real lift of the quotient is required to define the homotopy on all of G. Its discussion of overlap consistency and density extension supplies the same global well-definedness obligation identified by the gold issue.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The displayed interpolation F(t,x)=tf(x)+(1-t)g(x) does not define a representative-independent map into R/Z, and equality of winding numbers alone is insufficient without a compatible global real lift of f/g; consequently the converse homotopy construction is unsupported.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proposed homotopy must be representative-independent and globally well-defined, requiring a compatible real lift of the zero-winding quotient rather than merely equality of winding vectors.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that real scaling of T-valued values depends on representatives, that loopwise lifts do not establish a global map, that overlaps must be consistent, and that the repair is to use a real lift of g−f and verify consistency before extension. This independently diagnoses the full gold concern.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-010 recognizes the same construction-level defect: jumps are imposed using an embedded successor cycle while the theorem prescribes winding on the original level cycle, and the stated embedding conditions do not ensure that the jump computes the prescribed winding. It does not formulate the repair specifically as equality of homology classes or winding functionals, so the match is broader underlying weakness rather than exact causal identity.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The cycle embedding and cut construction do not establish that the jump placed on the successor/embedded cycle induces the prescribed winding on the original cycle. Thus the construction has not been shown to realize the theorem's specified degree vector; the prediction demonstrates this through the missing requirement that each cut lie on and be crossed by its own realizing loop, while the gold states the equivalent homology/winding-functional requirement.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: No substantive gold concern is left unrecognised; the prediction uses a geometric realization/cut-crossing formulation rather than the gold's homology-class formulation.

component_coverage.gold_component: The jump assigned using the successor embedded cycle is not shown to induce the prescribed winding on the original cycle, because the embedding/cut hypotheses do not establish the required correspondence of loops and winding functionals.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly distinguishes the level-m successor embedded cycle from the level-m prescribed cycle, states that vertex-set conditions do not ensure the cut lies on the intended loop or that other loops avoid it, and concludes that the jumps need not produce the prescribed winding. Its repair requires each cut to lie on its own realizing loop and to be crossed exactly by that loop, independently diagnosing the complete construction failure.
